newsitem.title: UK: BT issues another jumbo bond ahead of merger.
newsitem.headline: BT issues another jumbo bond ahead of merger.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc's $1.0 billion 10-year Eurobond, launched on Tuesday, was built on the success of a recent five-year offering, its group treasurer Andy Longden told Reuters.
"It was a follow-up exercise to the five-year, building on its success," he said. "Clearly the same circumstances apply as last time."

BT, which issued an extremely well-received $1.5 billion five-year Eurobond in April, said at the time that the launch was driven by its need for funds ahead of its merger with MCI Communications Corp.
As part of the merger to form Concert Plc, BT must make a cash payment of around $2.5 billion to MCI shareholders in September. BT will also offer shares to MCI shareholders.
BT also faces the prospect of having to finance a proposed "windfall" charge on its profits as part of the new British government's tax-raising plans.

While British finance minister Gordon Brown has not said since his Labour Party won power which privatised firms will be made to pay the tax, an increasing number of analysts believe BT will come within the tax's remit.
Today's 10-year deal was reoffered at a yield spread of 26 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, the level at which it was quoted on broker screens shortly after being freed to trade.

"We seem to have pitched it (spread) spot on," Longden said. "(Investor) sentiment is different at 10 years. Pricing needs to be more precise than at five years," he said, adding BT had no intention at present of increasing the size of the deal.
Its five-year bond, originally launched on April 8 as a $1.0 billion deal at a 15 b.p. spread and increased by $500 million on April 17, has tightened to nine b.p.
A key factor helping both deals, particularly last month's, was BT's relative rarity in Eurodollars. It had previously tapped the sector in July 1994.
BT is rated AA1 by Moody's Investors Service and may lose its AAA rating from Standard & Poor's Corp.
Dealers said the credit rating was perhaps less relevant than BT's future earning potential following the merger with MCI.

Concert wants to provide clients around the globe with local, long distance, international and mobile phone services as well as multi-media, internet-based services and systems integration for business clients.
After the merger the combined firm will be the second largest telecommunications company in the world with revenues of around $40 billion.
